instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires clients (principals) to file reports semi-annually (July 15 and January 15), not annually.
Client (principal) spending reports are due twice per year, not monthly.
The statute specifies semi-annual filing dates rather than an alternative 'other' periodic schedule.
The client report is due on July 15 and January 15, not quarterly.
Section 1-j(b) requires semi-annual reports filed by July 15 and January 15.
The statute requires semi-annual reporting, not tri-annual reporting linked to the legislative calendar.
The semi-annual client report must include the client's name, address and phone number, but it does not require disclosure of the nature of the client's business.
Clients must report 'the compensation paid or owed to each such lobbyist' for lobbying.
Clients must report 'the name of the person, organization, or legislative body before which such client has lobbied,' which constitutes disclosure of lobbying contacts.
The report must include 'a description of the general subject or subjects' on which lobbying occurred.

Clients must report 'any other expenses paid or incurred...for the purpose of lobbying' and itemize expenses over $75, which would include items like gifts/entertainment/transportation/lodging if incurred for lobbying (subject to stated exclusions).
In addition to lobbyist compensation, the client must disclose 'any other expenses paid or incurred...for the purpose of lobbying,' capturing non-compensation (indirect) costs.
Clients must disclose the 'name, address and telephone number of each lobbyist retained, employed or designated' by the client.
The semi-annual report must list each lobbyist retained, employed or designated by the client.
Certain high-spending clients must report 'the names of each source of funding over five thousand dollars from a single source' used to fund the lobbying and the amounts received.
The report must contain 'the name, address and telephone number of the client.'
The client report must include 'the legislative bill numbers of any bills' lobbied on.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: NY Legis L § 1-j(a); NY Legis L § 1-j(b)(5)(i) (2015)
instantiated_cells.justification: Clients required to file must report compensation paid/owed to each lobbyist and other lobbying expenses, which together constitute total client lobbying expenditures (including consulting and any reported in-house expenses).
Section 1-j requires the spending report to include the compensation paid or owed to each lobbyist, i.e., specific salary/fees paid.

Expenses must be aggregated only if $75 or less, but expenses over $75 must be detailed by amount, payee, and purpose (and name of beneficiary where applicable), requiring itemization for larger expenses.
The client semi-annual report lists the client and its lobbyists and expenditures but does not require listing all sponsors or members of associations or representative groups.
The client must report the name, address, and telephone number of each lobbyist retained, employed, or designated, thereby listing the lobbyists working for the principal.
